NO. 025 · Songbirds & City Birds / Pycnonotidae · Bulbuls

Red-whiskered Bulbul

红耳鹎 · hóng ěr bēi Pycnonotus jocosus
Resident Common 20–22 cm Protected (China) IUCN LC

A dandy in a black top hat with a dab of rouge

A tall black crest, a slash of scarlet on the cheek, and undertail coverts touched with vermilion. The Red-whiskered Bulbul is one of the most recognisable birds in a southern park, and the earliest alarm clock: it starts warming up from a high branch before the sky is light.

Gallery

One scientific illustration for shape and colour blocks, two field photographs for how it looks in real light. Click any image to enlarge.

Identification

  • CrestA long, pointed black crest that snaps upright into a small spire when the bird is excited — its most conspicuous feature.
  • CheekA vivid red patch below and behind the eye, the source of the name; its depth varies with age and mood.
  • PlumageUpperparts dark brown; throat white; a broken black band around the sides of the breast forming a collar; belly white; undertail coverts bright red.
  • TailLong, with white tips to the outer feathers, obvious as white corners when the tail is spread in flight.

Behaviour

Lively and restless, often standing upright on a branch looking about with the tail dipping. Keeps to small parties and often mixes with Light-vented Bulbuls. Eats fruit, nectar and insects, with a particular weakness for banyan figs and berries. The cup nest is usually 1–3 m up in a bush or foliage. More wary than the Light-vented Bulbul: as you approach it gives a short alarm first.

Voice

Field recording
Tap the waveform to seek · headphones recommended
0:00 / 0:55
Recording Subhashish Panigrahi · Licence CC BY-SA 4.0 · Original file

A clear, varied 'chu-chu, chu, chu' — rounder and bouncier than Light-vented Bulbul. The alarm is a dry, urgent chatter that tells you at once you have been noticed.

Where to find it in Zhuhai

  • Xiangshan Lake Park
  • Seaside Park
  • Qi'ao mangrove fringe
  • housing-estate green belts
Field note
Look at the hat: a tall pointed crest means Red-whiskered; a flat crown means Light-vented. They often share a tree, so use the voice to tell them apart.
